proposals.relationship: Wong traces his comparative historical social science and the initial framing of China Transformed to his training with Charles Tilly.
proposals.evidence_note: Own original 2017 Fudan interview, first and fourth answers, explicitly identifies Tilly’s historical social science as the work he wanted to do and his undergraduate training as the immediate reason for the Europe–China comparison. This is Wong’s retrospective statement of specific intellectual formation, not an inference from a shared university, an independently audited annual meeting chronology, or proof he adopted all of Tilly’s models. The displayed English answers ground the claim; the accompanying Chinese rendering is not treated as a separate interview or expanded quotation.
primary_locators: Original Fudan School of Economics interview, 19 May 2017, answers to “After graduating from the Department of Economics” and “Your influential book China Transformed”

proposals.relationship: Wong takes Braudel’s relational regional analysis as a resource for comparing Asian histories beyond national and Eurocentric frames.
proposals.evidence_note: Own 2001 article, translated into French by Pierre-Étienne Will, 5–9, especially 6 and 8–9, presents the Mediterranean as a framework between nation and globe and emphasizes changing human connections rather than fixed cultural boundaries. Wong distinguishes Braudel’s flexible, contingent regions from Skinner’s more enduring hierarchical macroregions while examining how Asian histories can use the approach. This is a particular analytic resource, not evidence that every Asian region is a Mediterranean replica or a newly read Braudel original. Note 1 specifies use of the 1966 edition; note 2 separately cites a 1976 manifestation. The publisher’s 2017 online migration date does not replace the original February 2001 issue date.
primary_locators: Annales HSS 56:1 (January–February 2001), selected printed 5–9, particularly 6/note 1 and 8–9; French translation by Pierre-Étienne Will
